<!-- Generated by `node scripts/docs-reference.mjs`. Do not edit. -->

At the default zoom a whole song fits on the screen and a single word is a few pixels wide. Zooming in lets you place the cursor exactly on a beat or in the gap between two words; zoom to selection frames just the passage you are working on.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **View → Zoom (Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3)**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Choose **View → Zoom → Zoom in**. Each step doubles the width of a second. Ctrl+1 does the same.
4. Choose **View → Zoom → Zoom in**.
5. Drag in the ruler above the clip, from the 40% mark to the 60% mark of the clip, to select that range. Select the passage you want to work on.
6. Choose **View → Zoom → Zoom to selection**. The selection now fills the timeline.
7. Choose **View → Zoom → Zoom normal**. Ctrl+2 brings the default zoom back.

## Tips

- Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom around the pointer, which is the quickest way to dive into one spot.
- Zooming changes nothing in the project; it is only your view.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
